turns.content: Hey, quick question. Gary gave me four binders of closed mediation cases to catalog by 5 PM. The master log is incomplete — some folders don't have case years and a bunch overlap topics. Should I group by year or by dispute type? And am I overthinking this or is he quietly benching me after those phone screw-ups yesterday

You’re not crazy for spinning on both of these at once. A messy filing job plus “did I just get benched” is a nasty combo, especially after a bad phone day.

**Cataloging:** don’t physically reshuffle four binders by 5. Catalog them. Make a simple log with: case name / parties, year (or `undated`), primary dispute type, other topics, binder number, and a one-line note. Sort the *log* however the office already thinks — if the master log is year-ish, keep it year-ish.

If you *have* to pick one grouping:
- **Year** is cleaner for closed files (archives, “when was this”). Put undated in their own bucket at the back. Don’t invent years.
- **Dispute type** is better if people actually pull these as examples later — but overlapping topics will eat your afternoon in “does this go in employment or contract.”

Missing years: peek at the first few pages for a date stamp, caption, or settlement date. If it’s not obvious in 30 seconds, `undated`. Overlaps: pick one primary type, list the rest in a topics column. No dual-filing.

If Gary is reachable, send two lines: “Defaulting to year + undated bucket, with dispute type as a column. Yell if you want type-first.” That reads like competence, not panic.

**The benching spiral:** this is probably not a quiet firing. Closed-case cataloging is grunt work, but it’s also contained, visible, and off the phones — which is a pretty normal “reset the day” move after screw-ups, not a verdict. Your brain is hunting for punishment; a binder pile isn’t proof. Knock this out clean, don’t over-apologize in the handoff, and let the work be the repair.

If you want, I can sketch the exact column headers so you can just copy them into the log.

Yeah the master log is sorted by year so I'll keep that. Undated goes in its own bucket

Column headers sound good what do you use

Use these — year first so it drops straight into the master log:

**Year** | **Case name / parties** | **Case no.** | **Closed / settlement date** | **Primary dispute type** | **Other topics** | **Binder** | **Folder / tab** | **Notes**

How to fill it without getting stuck:
- **Year** = the year you’re filing under. Undated = `undated` (own bucket, not guessed).
- **Closed / settlement date** = the actual date if you can snag it in ~30 seconds; otherwise leave blank.
- **Primary dispute type** = one label only (whatever the office already uses: employment, contract, landlord-tenant, etc.).
- **Other topics** = the overlap junk, comma-separated. Don’t dual-file.
- **Notes** = one line max: missing year, duplicate, weird caption, “see also X.”

If a folder has no case number, leave it blank. Don’t invent one.

Sort the log by **Year** (undated last), then case name. Leave the binders as they are unless Gary asked you to physically refile.
One more thing. The undated ones — a few have a mediator name and a handwritten date on the folder tab that doesn't match anything inside. Do I log the tab date or leave it blank

Leave the official date blank. Don’t file it under the tab year.

A tab date that doesn’t match anything inside is usually leftover labeling — reused folder, session date, intake scribble, wrong case. If you promote it to **Year** or **Closed / settlement date**, you’ll pollute the master log.

Log it like this:
- **Year:** `undated`
- **Closed / settlement date:** blank
- **Notes:** `tab date 3/14/19 (no match inside); mediator: [name]`

That’s enough that Gary can still find it, and you’re not inventing a year.

Only use a date from inside the file (caption, award, settlement, stamped correspondence). If the tab date *does* match something in the papers, then it’s real — use that date and skip the caveat.
Alright thanks. That saves me guessing. One more thing. When I hand this to Gary at 5 do I say anything about the phone mess yesterday or just hand him the log

Just hand him the log. Don’t reopen yesterday.

A clean handoff sounds like: “Master log’s updated by year. Undated are in their own bucket — tab dates that didn’t match the file are in notes, not used as the year. Overlaps got one primary type plus extra topics in the other column.” Then stop.

Bringing up the phones on your own turns a finished task into a confession. He already knows about yesterday. If he wants to talk about it, he’ll start it. If he doesn’t, you just showed him you can close a messy job without drama.

If he *does* bring it up: one short line, no speech. “Yeah, that was on me. I’ll be tighter on the phones.” Then get back to the binders.
Ok I think I can have it done by 430 if I skip lunch. When I hand it off do I tell Gary the undated bucket has five folders or just let him ask

Mention the five. Don’t wait for him to ask.

That’s not oversharing — it’s the one exception in a year-sorted log, and five folders is a number he can clock in two seconds. Skip lunch if you want the buffer, but the handoff itself should stay short.

Something like: “Log’s by year. Five undated — tab dates that didn’t match are in notes, not used as the year.” Then give him the log and stop.

Don’t add “I skipped lunch” or anything about yesterday. The five is useful; the rest is noise.
